name: r_unsupported_signature_scheme
description: attestation.scheme changed to a non-eip191 value; signature bytes themselves are UNTOUCHED and still recover correctly (scheme lives inside the attestation block, outside the signed preimage) — a VALID eip191 signature over a receipt declaring a different scheme. Verifier must fail closed as attestation_unsupported_scheme (distinct from attestation_invalid) rather than silently running eip191 recovery against an undeclared scheme; protocolEnforced1pct must be false even though every other check (split legs, contract binding) still passes.

name: s_scheme_null
description: attestation.scheme is JSON null (not a string at all). Verifier must fail closed identically to a wrong-string scheme — never let a non-string type reach the recovery call, and never let TS null/Python None formatting divergence leak into the detail string (both render the canonical token "null").

name: t_scheme_non_string_type
description: attestation.scheme is a JSON number (not a string). Same fail-closed requirement as null: type confusion in the scheme field must never reach eip191 recovery, and the detail string must render a fixed canonical marker (never language-native number stringification, which diverges between JS and Python for non-integer values).

name: u_scheme_newline_injection
description: attestation.scheme is a string containing an embedded newline and text shaped like a fake verifier output line (log/evidence-forging attempt). The verifier's own output IS the evidence, so unauthenticated attacker-controlled data must never be interpolated raw into it. Detail string must hex-escape the newline (\x0a) rather than emitting a literal line break.
